package_info.package_versions: Vulnerable versions prior to patched releases (see Microsoft advisory for specifics)
package_info.why_malicious: The malicious item exploits the PidLidReminderFileParameter MAPI property by setting it to an attacker-controlled UNC path. This causes Outlook to automatically initiate an NTLM authentication attempt to the attacker's SMB server, resulting in the silent leakage of the user's NTLMv2 hash without any user interaction.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when Outlook receives and processes the calendar or task item email)
execution_context.file_location: PidLidReminderFileParameter property within the Outlook calendar or task item (MAPI message property)
required_permissions: access to environment variables containing NTLM credentials

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, Outlook processes the calendar or task item and reads the PidLidReminderFileParameter property, which is set to a remote UNC path. Outlook then automatically attempts to fetch the specified sound file from the attacker's SMB share, causing the client to send NTLM authentication data over the network, resulting in the exfiltration of the user's NTLMv2 hash to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Assigning a reminder sound to an external, attacker-controlled UNC path is highly abnormal and directly causes Outlook to initiate an automatic NTLM authentication attempt, leaking sensitive credential hashes without any user action.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, reminder sounds are set to local files or trusted, internal network shares. Outlook is not expected to authenticate to arbitrary, untrusted external SMB servers automatically, especially without user interaction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some organizations may use internal network shares for reminder sounds, but these would be on trusted, internal servers—not external or internet-accessible hosts.
key_indicators: PidLidReminderFileParameter references an external or untrusted UNC path (e.g., \\IP-address\share or \\domain\share)
Automatic SMB/NTLM authentication attempts to external or non-corporate servers triggered by Outlook
Credential (NTLMv2 hash) leakage occurs without any user interaction
Calendar or task item contains a reminder sound property pointing to a non-local resource

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a calendar or task item with the PidLidReminderFileParameter property set to a malicious, external UNC path.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim receives the email, and Outlook processes the item, reading the malicious property.

attack_chain.action: Outlook automatically triggers the reminder, attempting to fetch the sound file from the specified UNC path.
attack_chain.leads_to: Outlook initiates an SMB/NTLM authentication attempt to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Victim's NTLMv2 hash is sent to the attacker's server via the SMB authentication process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker captures the NTLMv2 hash for offline cracking or relay attacks, potentially leading to further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Outlook calendar or task items with PidLidReminderFileParameter set to external or untrusted UNC paths
Automatic SMB/NTLM authentication attempts to external or non-corporate servers initiated by Outlook processes
NTLM credential leakage from user workstations without any user interaction, correlated with Outlook activity
file_indicators: MAPI messages where PidLidReminderFileParameter references \\external-server\share or any non-local UNC path
Calendar or task items with reminder sound properties set to network locations outside the trusted domain
network_indicators: Outbound SMB (port 445) connections from user workstations to external or untrusted IP addresses triggered by Outlook
NTLM authentication attempts from Outlook to servers outside the corporate network
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Outlook calendar or task items where the PidLidReminderFileParameter references an external or untrusted UNC path. Use email security tools to scan and quarantine items with suspicious reminder sound properties. Correlate SMB/NTLM authentication attempts from user workstations to external IPs with Outlook process activity. Block or alert on outbound SMB traffic to non-corporate destinations. Implement rules to flag MAPI messages with reminder sound properties pointing to non-local resources.
